clean_source_blocks.text: The fires broke out almost simultaneously on a Greek island near Athens on Sunday Two people have died and an evacuation is under way after two fires broke out within minutes of each other on a Greek island near Athens. Fire officials said nearly 200 firefighters were working to extinguish the flames on the island of Salamina and keep them from converging, Greek media report. The first blaze was reported at 14:40 local time (12:40 GMT) and spread rapidly due to high winds, according to officials on the island - which was under a high wildfire risk on Sunday. Some 90 people have so far been evacuated by sea, a coastguard spokesman told Greek broadcaster ERT. Five patrol boats have been sent to the area and several other private vessels are being made available for assistance, he added.
Nearly 200 firefighters are trying to keep the two fires on Salamina apart, Greek media report.

Many families are only just discovering the extent of damage to their homes for the first time. Nearly 200 firefighters are trying to keep the two fires on Salamina apart, Greek media report. Hundreds of firefighters are trying to contain the flames consuming the major park. Firefighters say they have had many calls but cannot tackle barbecues unless it is an emergency. The latest: Firefighters tackling a wildfire say they are focusing on extinguishing hotspots. Chief Fire Officer, Jon Pryce, said the service has attended 800 open fires in the county since May. The news comes after it was revealed the Red Arrows would not be able to make Eastbourne's Airbourne. The Cambridgeshire-based Rapid Relief Team provides refreshments and wipes to emergency services. Major incidents declared across England and Wales with blazes in Stourbridge, Sandwell and Pershore.

A number of aircraft and 50 fire engines have been deployed to the blaze. Salamina Deputy Mayor Thodoris Zannis said firefighters were trying to keep the fires from burning over a mountain on the island and forming one major wildfire. Salamina sits just west of Athens and has some 37,000 residents, many of them elderly. Firefighters across Europe have been facing a series of wildfires this weekend, fuelled by high heat. The fires broke out almost simultaneously on a Greek island near Athens on Sunday

Two people have died and an evacuation is under way after two fires broke out within minutes of each other on a Greek island near Athens.

Fire officials said nearly 200 firefighters were working to extinguish the flames on the island of Salamina and keep them from converging, Greek media report.

The first blaze was reported at 14:40 local time (12:40 GMT) and spread rapidly due to high winds, according to officials on the island - which was under a high wildfire risk on Sunday.

Some 90 people have so far been evacuated by sea, a coastguard spokesman told Greek broadcaster ERT.

Five patrol boats have been sent to the area and several other private vessels are being made available for assistance, he added.

A number of aircraft and 50 fire engines have been deployed to the blaze.

Salamina Deputy Mayor Thodoris Zannis said firefighters were trying to keep the fires from burning over a mountain on the island and forming one major wildfire.

Salamina sits just west of Athens and has some 37,000 residents, many of them elderly.
